summary: Repaired the fp16/bf16 reduction SIGILL class (24 LAUNCH_FAIL cases, native exit -4). Root cause (identified by walking one failing artifact and a 6-variant probe on the pinned QEMU): the emitted 'vmslt.vv v5, v2, v4' ran at SEW=64/LMUL=2 with the mask destination v5 STRICTLY INSIDE the vs2 register group v4-v5 -- an illegal-instruction form. Probed rule: a mask-destination compare traps when vd falls strictly inside an LMUL>1 source group; vd at the group's exact base (the fp32 artifacts' form) or disjoint is legal. The allocator had no constraint for mask destinations: the mixed-LMUL interference edge requires is_vector() on both sides and masks are not vectors, and dying source operands get no def-point edge. Fix in the SHARED allocation path (a100c/backend/allocate.py, no per-operator branch): _mask_compare_groups() maps each vcmp/vcmpx mask to its LMUL>1 operand groups; the coloring rejects strictly-inside candidates in BOTH directions (mask vs already-assigned operand groups, operand group vs already-assigned mask); _check_group_overlap() asserts the invariant after every successful coloring so a regression fails at compile time. Verification: all 36 cases of the six operators (amax, count_nonzero, mean, nansum, norm__max_norm, vector_norm__l1_norm; shapes 17/97/115; float32/float16/bfloat16) execute and compare PASS at 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers (formal reports at scan-final/threads-{1,2,4,8}); new regression test a100c/tests/test_t042_repairs.py reproduces the pre-fix placement with the constraint disabled and asserts the legal form (all checks PASS); fp32 (amax) and int8 (nanmedian histogram-count) reduction artifacts are instruction-stream-identical pre/post fix (only the revision comment and the assembler temp-filename in .debug_str differ) and execute PASS; full a100c test suite green (50/50, the compile sweep re-run with a proper bound); a 910-case reduction-family slice: 907 PASS + 3 TIMEOUTs that were the default 120s case budget vs this operator's legitimate ~210-232s cold compile (passes at the declared 240s scan timeout; pre-fix cold compile 219.2s vs post-fix 210.7s -- no compile-time regression).
